items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: Arstella had presented herself to me after a concert at the Edouard 7th theatre

ctx.x: I had been introduced to Jimmy by Beezie in 1940 because they were both from Leonia, New Jersey, and she had known him a long time before we met. Jimmie sang and accompanied himself on the piano. He had been a warrant officer in the army and came to France after his discharge.

In Geneva with Jack Dieval was Kenny Clarke on drums, Paul Vernon a French tenor man, Emmanuel Soudieux, also French, on bass, and an American Negro singer, named Arstella Whitter from Rochester, N.Y.

Arstella had presented herself to me after a concert at the Edouard 7th theatre, my first or second one, and told me that she knew a little girl in Rochester whom I called my niece but she actually was not related to me. I never knew how Arstella happened to come across to France,and as a singer. I had never heard of her in the States, but she had a nice voice in the style of Ella Fitzgerald, when she sang sweet numbers.
